summary: Turn algorithm contracts into independent bounded oracles, invariant checks, adversarial cases, minimized counterexamples, and honest proof limits.
triggers: An algorithm needs executable invariants or a reference oracle.
Boundary and adversarial cases should expose incorrect branches.
A failing example needs minimization and a durable regression guard.
antiTriggers: Claim a theorem from a finite test suite.
Implement against an unsettled input or output contract.
Derive expected results circularly from the candidate.

provenance.note: Method source read in full and independently rewritten for portable product use; the historical file remains unchanged.
Contract, independent oracle, counterexample, and proof-boundary semantics informed the rewrite; no source prose was copied.
Ownership and evidence boundaries were consulted; no algorithm qualification is asserted.
